findings.explanation: The repository guide's ASHRAE example also labels 18 to 27°C (about 64 to 80°F) as 'A1 OK', so the text agrees with the guide. ASHRAE TC 9.9 itself publishes that range as the recommended envelope and gives a wider allowable range for Class A1. Check which wording the catalogue should use.
findings.quote: Alert on exceedance of ASHRAE A1 limits (64-80°F intake).
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'ASHRAE recommended range (18-27°C / 64-80°F) at the rack inlet' and name the TC 9.9 edition, or align with the guide's labelling.

findings.explanation: dataSources include exhaust and ambient sensors, but the SPL applies one 64-80°F band to every event, while the implementation says the band is for intake. Hot-aisle or exhaust readings will exceed 80°F normally and alert constantly.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter the SPL by sensor position (intake only) or give separate thresholds per position.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no stats, no `entity` field and no count. It returns one row per out-of-range event.
findings.quote: grouped by `entity`. Outputs `count` each `the scheduled window`; alert when `temp_f` > 80, or `temp_f` < 64.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe one row per sensor reading outside 64-80°F, with zone, rack and sensor position.

findings.explanation: Boilerplate shared with every UC in the sub-category. The Universal Forwarder is not a Splunkbase app and has no sensor modular input. It names neither the SNMP source nor `sensor:temperature`, which is not in the guide's sourcetype list.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the SNMP add-on or collector and the fields `zone`, `rack`, `sensor_position`, `temp_f` that the SPL reads.

findings.explanation: Contradicts the earlier 'Poll via SNMP every minute'. The text also contains two overlapping procedures with the 'Step 4 — Operationalize' heading repeated four times, and a generic `earliest=-24h@h` schedule.
findings.quote: Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one numbered procedure with one polling interval and one search window.

findings.explanation: Search-time filters do not change Splunk licence usage, which is metered on indexed volume.
findings.quote: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost
findings.suggested_fix: Say early filters make the search cheaper to run.

findings.explanation: The HEC, inputs.conf and savedsearches.conf links are generic. Nothing covers ASHRAE temperature limits or the SNMP sensor feed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the ASHRAE TC 9.9 guidance and the sensor vendor or SNMP add-on documentation.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `index=environment` and `sourcetype="sensor:temperature"` are not in the guide's index list (the guide uses `dc_environmental`) or sourcetype list. Confirm which feed this reads.

summary: A simple per-sensor temperature search wrapped in template text. One 64-80°F band is applied to intake, exhaust and ambient sensors alike, and the ASHRAE wording is imprecise.
